title: Magic loop for small circumferences
subtitle: Working small rounds on a single long circular needle.
excerpt: The magic loop method uses a long circular needle (at least 80 cm) to knit small circumferences by pulling a loop of cable out at the side. One needle, one cable, no ladders at junction points.
sourceNotes: Magic loop technique widely documented in modern knitting literature. The principle of dividing stitches over a single long cable derives from earlier two-cable methods and is consistent with the circular needle mechanics described in twentieth-century British pattern books.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of knitting small circumferences in the round using a single long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint of the stitches, dividing them into two groups, and the work is rotated to knit each group in turn.

content.text: method knits any small circumference on a single circular needle at least 80 cm long by dividing the stitches into two groups and pulling a loop of spare cable out of the midpoint. There are no needle junctions to create ladders, no extra short needles to keep track of, and the same pair of needle tips serves the whole project. The method adapts to any circumference, including the tiny rounds of i-cord. Difficulty: intermediate.
One circular needle at least 80 cm long (100 cm is more comfortable)
Cast on the required number of stitches onto the circular needle.
Slide all stitches to the centre of the cable.

Fold the cable in half at the midpoint of the stitch count. Pull a loop of cable through at this fold, between two stitches. The cast-on is now divided: half the stitches sit on the needle tip in your right hand, half on the needle tip in your left.
Check that no stitches are twisted.
Slide the back (left) half of the stitches onto the left needle tip. The back needle tip should now extend freely behind the work.
Knit across the front stitches (the right-hand half) using the back needle tip as the working needle.
When the front group is complete, rotate the work 180 degrees. Pull the loop out again at the midpoint, slide the second group onto the left needle tip, and knit across.
Repeat: each half-round completes one group. Two half-rounds = one full round.

Magic loop is the standard method for sock knitting, used by knitters who prefer one set of needle tips over a set of DPNs. Hat crowns, glove fingers, and sweater yokes all use it once the stitch count drops too low for a short circular needle.

items.symptom: Tight ladder at the point where cable is pulled through
items.cause: The first stitch of each half is worked loosely when the cable is re-tensioned
items.fix: At the transition from cable to needle, snug the first stitch by pulling the working yarn firmly. Keep the first two stitches of each group slightly tighter than body tension.

items.symptom: Cable too stiff to pull into a loop
items.cause: Cheap or old plastic cable that does not flex easily
items.fix: Run the cable through warm hands before starting. A flexible cable (nylon-core circular needles) is far more comfortable for magic loop than a rigid plastic cable.

items.symptom: Lost track of which half is the start of the round
items.cause: No marker placed at the round start
items.fix: Place a locking stitch marker on the last stitch of the first half-round. When the marker reappears, you are at the round start.
